newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - July 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - July 19.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006 E-mail: biznis@giasdl01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
Indian Express
KARUNANIDHI TRIGGERS ANOTHER CONTROVERSY

Dravida Munnetra Kazagham (DMK) party chief M. Karunanidhi said no decision was taken at Thursday's core committee meeting on admitting the Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) party into the ruling United Front. He also said no decision was taken on the fate of the three ministers in the cabinet belonging to the RJD party. But the Communist Party of India-Marxist general secretary Harkishan Singh Surjeet, Janata Dal party president Sharad Yadav and former prime minister H.D. Deve Gowda said in New Delhi the decision not to admit the RJD party into the ruling Front was final. The controversy gave Rashtriya Janata Dal leader Laloo Yadav a chance to direct the three ministers not to resign from the cabinet.
The Economic Times
COUNTERVAILING DUTY ON CAPITAL GOODS IMPORT PLANNED

The Finance Ministry will soon give permission to levy 10 percent countervailing duty on import of capital goods under the export promotion of capital goods (EPCG) scheme. This forms part of the rationalisation of the EPCG scheme. The Central Board of Excise and Customs has already approved the proposal. The proposed countervailing duty is unlikely to be a disincentive to EPCG licence-holders as they will be allowed to avail of modified value added tax credits against the duty paid.
SLOWDOWN IN INDUSTRIAL GROWTH

The automobiles, steel, textile machinery, sugar, crude oil, power transformers sectors and about 10 other sectors registered negative growth in the first quarter of fiscal 1997/98 (April-March) according to growth figures compiled by the Confederation of Indian Industries (CII), based on feedback from affiliated industry associations and members. According to the CII, the constraints on industries include a resource crunch, infrastructure constraints, low investor confidence due to political uncertainties, an inverted duty structure and depressed demand.
Financial Express
EUROPEAN UNION DRAGS INDIA TO WTO DISPUTE SETTLEMENT FORUM

The European Union on Friday formally moved the dispute settlement body of the World Trade Organisation seeking consultations with India on phasing out quantitative restrictions on imports. This followed a breakdown of multilateral consultations in the WTO balance of payments committee. At the consultations on June 30 and July 1, India insisted that quantitative restrictions on imports were absolutely necessary to maintain its balance of payments position. The United States, Australia and New Zealand have already sought consultation with India under the dispute settlement body of the WTO.
CABINET ACCEPTS FIFTH PAY PANEL REPORT

The government on Friday accepted the fifth pay commission report which recommends higher pay scales for central government employees. The government accepted the modified report improving payscales in four categories and an increase in the ceiling on gratuity. But the cabinet rejected recommendations to raise the retirement age of central government employees to 60 years from 58 years, return to a six-day week and reduce government holidays. It also rejected the suggestion to make allowance and pension net of taxes. The joint consultative machinery representing central government employees rejected the package and threatened to go on strike.
BANK OFFICERS DEMAND SHARP HIKE IN BASIC PAY

About three million bank officers are demanding an increase in their basic pay from 4,250-14,000 rupees to 15,000-60,000 rupees. Four unions of the bank officers submitted a common charter of demands to the Indian Banks Association on Friday. The existing settlement will end in October 1997. The officers' unions demand a pay structure on the lines of the fifth pay commission's recommendations. The increase in basic pay is imperative to check talented people leaving government banks, said a union leader.
Business Standard
RESERVE BANK STEPS IN TO SAVE DOLLAR

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Friday bought about $250 million in the spot and forward markets to check a rise in rupee value against the dollar after it crossed 35.70. The rupee closed at 35.7150 against the dollar. Market sources said the RBI bought around $50 million to $60 million in the spot market and another $150 million to $200 million in the forward market. Intervention for the RBI is becoming increasingly difficult as the system is flush with funds and any further buying will increase the money supply, which will fuel inflation.
GOVERNMENT MAY ABSORB OIL POOL DEFICIT

The oil pool deficit, which stands at 190 billion rupees and is widening, is likely to be absorbed by the government into its own account in phases. Of this, 90 billion rupees will be absorbed during fiscal 1997/98 (April-March). The previous amount outstanding of 155 billion rupees will be absorbed over three to five years. This is likely to be done by issuing bonds which will be redeemed in phases. Ministry sources said the absorption of the oil deficit, indicated by the prime minister, was subject to the approval of the standing committee.
The Observer
VYSYA BANK TO GIVE 5 PCT MORE TO BELGIAN BANK

Vysya Bank shareholders have approved a proposal to allot 927,600 shares to Belgium-based private bank Brussels Lambert at 197 rupees a share. The scrip is quoted in the secondary market at around 160 rupees a share. Brussels Lambert entered into a strategic alliance with Bangalore-based Vysya Bank last year and took five percent of the expanded equity at 326 rupees a share when the market value was 151 rupees and the book value 235 rupees.
